name: Alcohol
aliases: alcohol, ethanol, ethyl alcohol, ethanol of agricultural origin, alcohol etílico, alcohol de origen agrícola
what_is: Ethanol is the alcohol found in alcoholic beverages and can also be used in foods as an ingredient, solvent or flavour carrier. This fiche applies when alcohol or ethanol is explicitly declared on the label.
why_botia: Ethanol is metabolised to acetaldehyde, which can damage DNA, and alcohol can also alter oestrogen levels involved in breast carcinogenesis. IARC classifies alcoholic beverage consumption and ethanol in alcoholic beverages as carcinogenic to humans (Group 1) and has established a causal relationship with female breast cancer; WHO notes that female breast-cancer risk increases even at relatively low levels of alcohol consumption, while a label declaration alone does not quantify exposure. BOTIA therefore activates the Woman layer; separately, its Muslim layer classifies an explicitly declared alcohol ingredient as Haram, without explaining or interpreting religious doctrine.
can_1: Detect explicitly declared alcohol, ethanol, ethyl alcohol and closely related label terms.
can_2: Explain why the Woman layer is activated from WHO/IARC evidence and report BOTIA's Muslim classification for an explicit alcohol declaration without interpreting religious doctrine.
cannot_1: Determine the amount of ethanol present or an individual's cancer risk from the ingredient declaration alone.
cannot_2: Infer undeclared alcohol, interpret religious doctrine or advise a person whether they should consume a product.

sources.label: WHO — Alcohol and breast cancer in women
